'''Atta-ur-Rahman''' ([[Urdu]]: عطاالرحمان; b. 22 September 1942), {{postnominals|list=[[Nishan-e-Imtiaz|NI]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|FPAS]]|country=PAK}} is a Pakistani [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]] currently serving as [[professor emeritus]] at the [[International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences]] at the [[University of Karachi]] and as Chairman of the Prime Minister 's Task Force on Science and Technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.pakistantoday.com.pk/2019/02/22/cabinet-approves-task-force-on-science-and-tech/|title=Cabinet approves task force on science and tech &#124; Pakistan Today|date=22 February 2019 |access-date=3 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182232/https://archive.pakistantoday.com.pk/2019/02/22/cabinet-approves-task-force-on-science-and-tech/|url-status=live}}</ref> He has twice served as the President of Pakistan Academy of Sciences (2003–2006, and 2011–2014).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.paspk.org/former-office-bearers/ | title=Pakistan Academy of Sciences &#124; Former Office Bearers }}</ref> He was the Federal Minister of Science and Technology (2000–2002), Federal Minister of Education (2002) and Chairman Higher Education Commission with status of Federal Minister (2002–2008)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.interacademies.org/person/atta-ur-rahman | title=Atta-ur Rahman }}</ref> He is also the President of the Network of Academies of Sciences in Countries of the Organisation of Islamic Countries (NASIC).<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasic.org.pk/|title=Network of Academies of Sciences in Countries of Organization of Islamic Conference - Home|website=www.nasic.org.pk}}</ref> After returning to Pakistan from Cambridge after completing his tenure as Fellow of Kings College, Cambridge University, he contributed to the development of the International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences at the University of Karachi, and transforming the landscape of higher education, science and technology of Pakistan. He is Fellow of Royal Society (London),  Life Fellow of Kings College, Cambridge University, UK,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/fellows/fellows-directory/ 
|access-date=14 April 2023|website=Royal Society|title=Fellows directory}}</ref> Academician Chinese Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite web | url=http://casad.cas.cn/ysxx2022/wjys/201512/t20151224_4502768.html | title=外籍院士名单与简介----中国科学院学部与院士 }}</ref> and professor emeritus at University of Karachi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Atta-Rahman-13|title=Atta RAHMAN &#124; Professor Emeritus &#124; PhD (Cambridge), DSc (Cambridge), DSc (Coventry), &#124; University of Karachi, Karachi &#124; HEJ Research Institute of Chemistry &#124; Research profile|accessdate=20 August 2023}}</ref>

==Education==
Atta-ur-Rahman was born on 22 September 1942 in [[Old Delhi]] into an [[Urdu-speaking]] academic family.<ref name=muslimscience>{{Cite web|title=Profiles in Leadership (3): Atta ur Rahman on HEJ, HEC, and OIC Science Cooperation Muslim Science|url=https://muslim-science.com/profiles-in-leadership-3-a-conversation-with-atta-ur-rahman-on-hej-hec-and-oic-science-cooperation/|access-date=2022-11-20|date=2011-04-11|first=Athar|last=Osama|website=Muslim Science}}</ref> His grandfather, Sir Abdur Rahman, was a [[vice-chancellor]] of the [[University of Delhi]] (1934–38) who briefly served as a [[British judges|judge]] at the [[Madras High Court]].<ref name="Arkat Foundation">{{cite web|date=22 September 2007|title=A Tribute to a Living Legend|url=http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/19766/|publisher=Arkat Foundation (US)|access-date=9 April 2021|archive-date=29 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210829053035/http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/19766/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1946, Abdur Rahman was appointed as vice-chancellor of the [[Punjab University, Lahore|Punjab University]] in [[Lahore]], eventually relocating his family there, a year before the [[partition of India]] took place.<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/> Abdur Rahman eventually became a [[List of Justices of the Supreme Court of Pakistan|Senior Justice]] at the [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|Supreme Court]] of [[Pakistan]] in 1949.<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/> His father, Jamil-ur-Rahman, was a [[Civil law (legal system)|lawyer]] who established a cotton ginning [[Textile industry in Pakistan|textile industry]] in [[Okara, Pakistan|Okara]], [[Punjab, Pakistan]].<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/> After settling in [[Karachi]] in 1952, he passed the competitive [[O-Level]] and [[GCE Advanced Level|A-Level]] from the [[Karachi Grammar School]] and joined [[Karachi University]].<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/>

Attending Karachi University in 1960, Rahman graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|bachelor's degree]] (with [[BSc (Hons)|honors]]) in chemistry in 1963.<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/><ref name="Pakistan Herald (Biography)">{{cite web |last1=Staff writer |title=Prof Dr Atta-ur-Rahman |work=Pakistan Herald |url=http://www.pakistanherald.com/profile/prof-dr-atta-ur-rahman-430 |access-date=28 February 2015 |publisher=Pakistan Herald (Biography) |archive-date=6 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150506191350/http://www.pakistanherald.com/profile/Prof-Dr-Atta-ur-Rahman-430 |url-status=live }}</ref> He obtained a [[Master of Science]] (MSc) in [[organic chemistry]] in 1964 with first class and 1st position, and lectured at Karachi University for a year before receiving a [[Commonwealth Scholarship]] for doctoral studies in the United Kingdom.<ref name="Arkat Foundation"/> He joined [[King's College, Cambridge|King's College]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] and resumed research in [[natural product]]s under John Harley-Mason.<ref name="Pakistan Herald (Biography)"/> In 1968, Rahman received a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) in [[organic chemistry]]; the subjects of his [[doctoral thesis]] were natural products and [[organic materials]].<ref name="Cambridge">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Atta-ur-Rahman, FRS |url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/ben/coc/2015/00000019/00000002/art00002?crawler=true |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703113114/https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/ben/coc/2015/00000019/00000002/art00002?crawler=true |archive-date=3 July 2020}}</ref><ref name="Arkat Foundation"/> He was elected as a fellow of King's College, University of Cambridge in 1969 and continued his research at Cambridge University until 1973.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/content/search/text?search_api_views_fulltext=Atta-ur-rahman |title=Search &#124; King's College Cambridge |publisher=Kings.cam.ac.uk |date=2021-09-17 |accessdate=2022-04-23 |archive-date=9 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709181829/https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/content/search/text?search_api_views_fulltext=Atta-ur-rahman |url-status=live }}</ref> During that period, he is credited with correcting the earlier work of the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|Nobel]] Laureate Sir [[Robert Robinson (chemist)|Robert Robinson]] on the chemistry of [[harmaline]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1 January 1972 |title=Reactions of harmaline (4,9-dihydro-7-methoxy-1-methyl-3H-pyrido[3,4-b]indole) and its derivatives. Part II. Reinvestigation of acetylharmaline |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1972/p1/p19720000736 |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1 |pages=736–738 |doi=10.1039/P19720000736 |via=pubs.rsc.org|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Later in 2007, he was appointed as an honorary life fellow of King's College Cambridge.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/research/fellows/honorary-fellows |title=Honorary Fellows &#124; King's College Cambridge |publisher=Kings.cam.ac.uk |date=2021-08-27 |accessdate=2022-04-23 |archive-date=9 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182415/https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/research/fellows/honorary-fellows |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Academic career==
In 1964, Rahman joined the [[University of Karachi|Karachi University]] as a [[Graduate assistant|lecturer]] in undergraduate [[chemistry]].<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences">{{cite web|last1=Pakistan Academy of Sciences |title=Profile of Fellow |url=http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=86 |publisher=Pakistan Academy of Sciences |access-date=28 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150121105405/http://www.paspk.org/detail.php?id=16&id1=86 |archive-date=21 January 2015  }}</ref> He remained associated with the [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]] between 1969 and 1973, and is presently honorary Life Fellow at the King's College of the Cambridge University.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> In 1977, he became the co-director of the [[Hussain Ebrahim Jamal Research Institute of Chemistry]] at [[University of Karachi]]; eventually he was ascended as the Director in 1990.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> In 1979, Rahman did the [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doctoral]] research at the University of Tübingen. Upon returning to Pakistan, he joined Karachi University where he lectures and taught chemistry.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences"/> He was appointed professor emeritus at University of Karachi for life.<ref name="uok.edu.pk">[http://www.uok.edu.pk/admissions/2015/basr/msmdprospectus.pdf Archived copy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207072144/http://www.uok.edu.pk/admissions/2015/basr/msmdprospectus.pdf |date=7 February 2017 }}</ref>

He carried out important studies on the synthesis of anti-cancer alkaloids present in the plant Catharanthus roseus and analytical studies on organic compounds involving circular dichroism and is generally recognized as bringing a huge positive change in the development of science and technology as well as higher education in Pakistan.<ref name="royalsociety.org">{{Cite web |title=Atta Ur Rahman |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/atta-ur-rahman-12136/ |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Choudhary |first=Muhammad Iqbal |date=14 March 2013 |title=Professor Atta-ur-Rahman: towering scientific achievements |journal=Natural Product Research |volume=27 |issue=4–5 |pages=298–301 |doi=10.1080/14786419.2013.766053 |pmid=23473069 |s2cid=19648663|doi-access= }}</ref>

His book entitled "Stereoselective Synthesis in Organic Chemistry" (Springer-Verlag) was termed a monumental contribution in the field by the Nobel Laureate Sir Derek Barton in the foreword of the book written by him.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BJfbBwAAQBAJ&q=stereoselective+synthesis+in+organic+chemistry,+foreword,+springer-verlag,+barton |title=Stereoselective Synthesis in Organic Chemistry |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=9781461383277 |via=Google Books}}</ref> His book entitled "NMR Spectroscopy-Basic Principles" was published by [[Springer-Verlag]] and translated into Japanese for use in university courses in Japan.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NGcdNgAACAAJ |title=Nuclear Magnetic Resonance: Basic Principles |date=14 November 1986 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |isbn=9783540962434 |via=Google Books}}</ref>  The Nobel Laureate [[Herbert C. Brown]] applauded the contributions of Rahman in science and technology.<ref>{{Cite web |last=imedia.com.pk |first=Interactive Media Pakistan- |title=International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences |url=https://www.iccs.edu/page-remarks-of-eminent-scientist |website=www.iccs.edu}}</ref>

Research Institute of Chemistry]] at Karachi University (2012)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://iccs.edu/page-hej | title=International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences | access-date=23 January 2018 | archive-date=31 January 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131211538/http://iccs.edu/page-hej | url-status=live }}</ref>

* Federal Minister of Science & Technology (2000–2002)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://most.comsatshosting.com/federalMinisters.aspx | title=Federal Ministers | access-date=23 January 2018 | archive-date=29 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029084542/http://most.comsatshosting.com/federalMinisters.aspx | url-status=live }}</ref>
* Federal Minister of Education (2002)<ref name="unesco.org">[http://www.unesco.org/new/fileadmin/MULTIMEDIA/HQ/SC/pdf/Flyer-Lecture_Pakistan_WSD14.pdf Profile of Atta-ur-Rahman on UNESCO.org website] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519070155/http://www.unesco.org/new/fileadmin/MULTIMEDIA/HQ/SC/pdf/Flyer-Lecture_Pakistan_WSD14.pdf |date=19 May 2017 }} Published 10 November 2014, Retrieved 9 April 2021</ref><ref>[http://sites.nationalacademies.org/cs/groups/pgasite/documents/webpage/pga_061771.pdf Archived copy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402135131/http://sites.nationalacademies.org/cs/groups/pgasite/documents/webpage/pga_061771.pdf |date=2 April 2015 }}</ref>
* Federal Minister/Chairman, [[Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)|Higher Education Commission]], Pakistan (resigned due to govt issues)(2002–2008)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref name="unesco.org"/>
* Advisor to the [[Prime Minister of Pakistan]] on [[Science]] and [[Technology]] (2002–2008)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://findmyhero.com/dr-atta-ur-rehman/ | title=Dr. Atta Ur Rehman | access-date=23 January 2018 | archive-date=28 February 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228200250/http://findmyhero.com/dr-atta-ur-rehman/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

==Government work and political advocacy==
After securing the [[Fellow of the Pakistan Academy of Sciences|fellowship]] of the [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]], Rahman had been affiliated with the [[Government of Pakistan|Pakistan government]] regarding [[Education in Pakistan|education]] and [[Science in Pakistan|science]] affairs.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> From 1996 until 2012, Rahman served in the [[board of directors]] of the [[Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation]], representing Pakistan's delegation.<ref name="Pakistan Academy of Sciences" /> In 1997, Rahman served as the Coordinator General of the [[Organisation of Islamic Cooperation]]'s (OIC) [[Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation]] (COMSTECH) that comprised 57 Ministers of Science and Technology from 57 OIC member countries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iccs.edu/pcmd/executive_board.php |title=Executive Board of ICCBS |access-date=10 November 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130520234530/http://www.iccs.edu/pcmd/executive_board.php |archive-date=20 May 2013  }}</ref> In recognition of his scientific transformation of Pakistan and building a large number of Centers of Excellence in the country as well as promoting scientific research, Rahman was conferred the TWAS Prize in Institution Building, in Durban, South Africa in 2009.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |title=Rahman, Atta-ur- |url=https://twas.org/directory/rahman-atta-ur |website=TWAS}}</ref> Atta-ur-Rahman has served as the co-chairman of UN ESCAP.<ref name="auto5">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Atta-Ur-Rahman – IAS |url=https://iasworld.org/fellows-cpt/prof-atta-ur-rahman/}}</ref>

In 1999, he joined the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Pakistan)|Ministry of Science and Technology]] (MoSci) as its [[Minister (government)|minister]], assisting in drafting the official science policy of the country. In 2002, he was appointed as minister of the [[Ministry of Education (Pakistan)|Ministry of Education]] (MoEd) as well as becoming the chairman of the [[Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)|Higher Education Commission]] (HEC) until resigning in 2008.<ref name="SUPARCO">{{cite web|last1=Staff work |title=Prof. Atta-ur-Rahman, FRS |url=http://www.suparco.gov.pk/pages/poeprofile/Prof%20Dr%20Atta.pdf |publisher=SUPARCO |access-date=28 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402090108/http://www.suparco.gov.pk/pages/poeprofile/Prof%20Dr%20Atta.pdf |archive-date=2 April 2015  }}</ref> Atta-ur-Rahman has also served as Chairman of the Prime Ministers National Task Force on Science and Technology, Co Chairman of Prime Ministers National Task Force on Information Technology and Telecommunications,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://moitt.gov.pk/NewsDetail/ZTI0NmNlNDgtZjg0Yi00ZDM0LWIxNDEtMGZiYTBmNzEwNjQ5 | title=Ministry of Information Technology & Telecommunication }}</ref> and Vice Chairman of the Prime Ministers Task Force on Technology Driven Knowledge Economy<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web |last=Partnership (IAP) |first=the InterAcademy |title=Atta-ur Rahman |url=https://www.interacademies.org/person/atta-ur-rahman |website=www.interacademies.org}}</ref> during the years 2019 to 2022. He is the President of the Network of Science of Organisation of Islamic Countries (NASIC).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.interacademies.org/organization/network-academies-science-countries-organisation-islamic-conference-nasic#:~:text=The%20Network%20of%20Academies%20of%20Sciences%20in%20OIC,development%20of%20S%26T%20programs%20among%20OIC%20member%20countries. | title=Network of Academies of Science in Countries of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (NASIC) }}</ref>

|url=https://cpecinfo.com/hunan-university-of-china-to-establish-professor-atta-ur-rehman-medicine-research-centre/}}</ref> as well as the Atta-ur-Rahman School of Applied Biosciences at the [[National University of Sciences and Technology (Pakistan)|National University of Sciences & Technology]] (Islamabad, Pakistan)<ref>{{Cite web |title=WELCOME TO ASAB – National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) |url=https://asab.nust.edu.pk/about-us/welcome-to-asab/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116182112/https://asab.nust.edu.pk/about-us/welcome-to-asab/ |archive-date=16 November 2022 |access-date=20 October 2022}}</ref> and the Atta-ur-Rahman Laboratories, International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences at the University of Karachi (Karachi, Pakistan).<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=imedia.com.pk |first=Interactive Media Pakistan- |title=International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences |url=https://www.iccs.edu/ |website=www.iccs.edu}}</ref> The US Publisher ARKAT USA has published a special issue of the journal [[Arkivoc]], Vol 2007, in honour of Atta-ur-Rahman FRS which had contributions from top scientists in the field of natural product chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archived copy |url=http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/19525/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109064658/http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/19525/ |archive-date=9 November 2022 |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref> Similarly, the [[International Journal of Molecular Sciences|international journal Molecules]] published by the Swiss publisher [[MDPI|MDP]]I published a special issue of the journal in honour of Atta-ur-Rahman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Molecules |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/molecules/special_issues/molecules_Atta-ur-Rahman |website=www.mdpi.com}}</ref> [[The World Academy of Sciences]], [[Italy]] has introduced a special Prize in his honour (TWAS-Atta-ur-Rahman Award in Chemistry) for young scientists which is awarded once every two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TWAS-Atta-ur-Rahman Award in Chemistry |url=https://twas.org/opportunity/twas-atta-ur-rahman-award-chemistry |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=[[The World Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref> In recognition of his eminent contributions, Prof. Atta-ur-Rahman has received honorary doctorate degrees from many universities including the University of Cambridge (UK), Coventry University (UK), Bradford University (UK), Universiti Teknologi Mara (Malaysia), Asian Institute of Teknologi (Thailand), University of Karachi (Pakistan), Gomal University (Pakistan), and several other universities.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://twas.org/directory/rahman-atta-ur | title=Rahman, Atta-ur- }}</ref>

===National and international Awards===
In recognition of his eminent contributions in the field of [[organic chemistry]], he has been conferred with many civil awards, including:
* [[Nishan-e-Imtiaz]] (2002) (highest national civil award)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref name="TNI">{{cite news |date=23 October 2011 |title=Malaysian King confers degree on Atta-ur-Rahman |newspaper=The News International (newspaper) |url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/Todays-News-4-73967-Malaysian-King-confers-degree-on-Atta-ur-Rahman |url-status=dead |access-date=7 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219073519/http://www.thenews.com.pk/Todays-News-4-73967-Malaysian-King-confers-degree-on-Atta-ur-Rahman |archive-date=19 December 2013}}</ref><ref name="unesco.org"/><ref name="auto5" />
* [[Hilal-e-Imtiaz]] (1998)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref name=TNI/><ref name="unesco.org"/>
* [[Sitara-e-Imtiaz]] (1991)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref name=TNI/><ref name="unesco.org"/>
* [[Tamgha-e-Imtiaz]] (1983)<ref name=Cambridge/><ref name=TNI/><ref name="unesco.org"/>
* [[UNESCO Science Prize]] (1999)<ref name="royalsociety.org"/><ref name="auto4" />
* [[Decoration of Honour for Services to the Republic of Austria|Grosse Goldene Ehrenzeischen am Bande]](2007) high civil award by the [[Government of Austria|Austrian government]] (2007)<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://twas.org/sites/default/files/member/brief_cv_prof._atta_july_2015.pdf|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221023064900/https://twas.org/sites/default/files/member/brief_cv_prof._atta_july_2015.pdf|url-status=dead|title=Archived copy|archivedate=23 October 2022}}</ref>
* China, International Science and Technology Cooperation Award (2020) bestowed by [[President of China|Chinese President]] [[Xi Jinping]] in Beijing on January 7, 2020<ref name="cpecinfo.com">{{cite web | last1=Shakeel | first1=Sharza | url=https://cpecinfo.com/dr-atta-ur-rehman-receives-the-china-international-science-and-technology-cooperation-award-2020/ | title=Dr. Atta-ur-Rehman receives the China International Science and Technology Cooperation Award 2020 | work=China Pakistan Economic Corridor | date=11 January 2020 }}</ref>
* Academician, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (2015)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Foreign Members---Academic Divisions of the Chinese Academy of Sciences |url=http://english.casad.cas.cn/mem/fm/ |website=english.casad.cas.cn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.interacademies.org/person/atta-ur-rahman|title=Atta-ur Rahman|first=the InterAcademy|last=Partnership (IAP)|website=www.interacademies.org|accessdate=14 April 2023}}</ref>
* Friendship Award of China (2014)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nation.com.pk/18-Sep-2014/dr-atta-ur-rahman-honoured | title=Dr Atta-ur-Rahman honoured | date=18 September 2014 }}</ref>
* Vice President, [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS)<ref name="auto2" />
* Prescient, Network of Academies of Science of Organising of Islamic Conference (NASIC)<ref name="auto3" />
* Member, [[Korean Academy of Science and Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://kast.or.kr/en/member/info.php?level=&keyfield=&search_order=rahman |title=한림원 - Member - Member Directory |access-date=16 November 2022 |archive-date=16 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116182104/https://kast.or.kr/en/member/info.php?level=&keyfield=&search_order=rahman&ckattempt=2 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Einstein Professorship, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="auto1" />
*  Babai Urdu Award (1994)<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.slideshare.net/TahirShahzad17/dr-atta-ur-rehman-85060506| title=Dr atta ur rehman| date=27 December 2017| access-date=23 January 2018| archive-date=24 August 2022| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220824054804/https://www.slideshare.net/TahirShahzad17/dr-atta-ur-rehman-85060506| url-status=live}}</ref>
*  Scientist of the Year Award (for 1985)/Prize Rs. 200,000 (1987)<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.slideshare.net/Jawad_Ahmad/dr-atta-ur-rahman| title=Dr Atta ur Rahman| date=13 May 2017| access-date=23 January 2018| archive-date=24 August 2022| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220824054356/https://www.slideshare.net/Jawad_Ahmad/dr-atta-ur-rahman| url-status=live}}</ref>
*  FPCCI Prize for Technological Innovation (1985)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://prideofpakistan.com/detail-who-is-who.php?name=DrAtta-ur-Rahman&id=88 |title=Dr. Atta-ur-Rahman &#124; Pride of Pakistan &#124; Scientists |publisher=PrideOfPakistan.com |date= |accessdate=2022-04-23 |archive-date=23 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180123190643/http://prideofpakistan.com/detail-who-is-who.php?name=DrAtta-ur-Rahman&id=88 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*  Engro Excellence Award (2010)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://atta-ur-rahman.com/engro-excellence-awards-2010-dr-atta-ur-rahman/ |title=Engro Excellence Awards 2010 |access-date=23 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124005732/http://atta-ur-rahman.com/engro-excellence-awards-2010-dr-atta-ur-rahman/ |archive-date=24 January 2018 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>
*  HEC, National Distinguished Professor (2011–present)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/HEC+gives+title+of+Distinguished+National+Professor+to+four+scholars-a0250384604|title=Higher Education Commission of Pakistan (HEC) gives title of Distinguished National Professor to four scholars|website=Free Online Library website|date=2011|access-date=7 April 2021|archive-date=15 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615031256/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/HEC+gives+title+of+Distinguished+National+Professor+to+four+scholars-a0250384604|url-status=live}}</ref>
*  Professor Emeritus, University of Karachi (2011–present)<ref name="uok.edu.pk"/>
* Lifetime Achievement Award by [[University of Management and Technology, Lahore]] (2012)
